concerns.text: T007 requires the schema to include per-step field `peak_memory_mb`, but the read-only contract (contracts/training_run.schema.yaml) names the per-step field `step_peak_memory_mb` and reserves `peak_memory_mb` for the run summary. An implementer following T007 verbatim will produce a schema that conflicts with the contract the task says it must match ('match the read-only contract provided in the active data model'), making the task's own verification (schema validation of logger output) fail. Rename the per-step field to `step_peak_memory_mb`.

T011 instructs: 'If CPU loading genuinely fails ... the script raises the exception so the execution stage can off-load to a real GPU (device="cuda")'. This gives the implementer a contradictory directive (FR-009 mandates abort-and-fail on any GPU fallback) and an unexecutable escape hatch on a CPU-only runner. The task must specify abort-and-report-failure behavior only, so the implementer has a deterministic action on load failure.

T012's teacher fallback chain (Qwen2.5-7B 8-bit, falling back to 3B) is not executable under the plan's own <7 GB RAM constraint on the target runner: a 7B 8-bit teacher (~7 GB weights alone) plus student and retriever cannot load. The task names no authorized teacher model from plan/spec (plan names only Qwen2.5-0.5B as student; no teacher size is specified anywhere), so the implementer cannot determine a feasible teacher configuration. Specify a teacher model that fits the memory budget or cite the authorizing spec/plan text.

T014 is too coarse for deterministic execution: it bundles 30 full training runs across 3 variants × 2 environments, plus a separate cost-only fixed-step sub-phase, in one task with no step count for the cost-only runs and no per-run invocation commands. Split into (a) the main grid execution and (b) the cost-only sub-phase with an explicit fixed step count, so each has a discrete verifiable deliverable.

T016 bundles two scripts (analyze_results.py, compare_variants.py), six report fields, and a noise-robustness perturbation experiment into one task. The noise-robustness check in particular lacks concrete parameters (what noise distribution/magnitude perturbs the retrieved chunks, how many runs are perturbed), so an implementer cannot execute it deterministically. Specify the perturbation procedure or split it into its own task.

T013's verification requires '≥ 100 paired real gating scores' but the task does not specify which baseline runs supply the trajectories or the minimum trajectory length, and depends on T012's teacher model being resolvable (see T012 concern). Add the source-run selection rule so the ≥100-pair threshold is checkable.
